chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer in the Ka'bah. He said: 'Between the two pillars, stand upon the red marble slab, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed upon it. Then he turned towards the corners of the House and pronounced Takbeer towards each corner from it.'

key_terms.الْبَلَاطَةِ الْحَمْرَاءِ: The red marble slab, a specific spot inside the Ka'bah
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Ka'bah, the cube-shaped building in Mecca

ai.seo_question: Where exactly should one stand when praying inside the Ka'bah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* establishes the specific spot of prayer (*musta'*) within the Ka'bah as the red marble slab (*al-balata al-hamra’*) located between the two pillars, affirming its status through the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) practice. It highlights the scholarly tradition of identifying precise physical markers for ritual validity, noting that the Prophet faced each corner (*arkān*) individually while standing on this slab, a detail often discussed in fiqh regarding the orientation of prayer inside the sanctuary.
